lesson_scope: Line meets curve intersections, tangents, and misses: simultaneous equations yielding quadratics, discriminant conditions for tangency ($b^2 - 4ac = 0$), non-intersection ($b^2 - 4ac < 0$), and two distinct points of intersection ($b^2 - 4ac > 0$), quadratic substitutions with square roots, and rational curve tangencies.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving simultaneous equations between a linear line and a parabola to find two intersection points.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of finding two intersection points of line and curve.

hints: Rearrange to $x^2 - x - 2 = 0$ and factorise as $(x - 2)(x + 1) = 0$.
Substitute $x = 2 \implies y = 4$ and $x = -1 \implies y = 1$ to get $(-1, 1)$ and $(2, 4)$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the expressions for $y$ and form a quadratic equation:
$$x^2 = x + 2$$
$$x^2 - x - 2 = 0$$
$$(x - 2)(x + 1) = 0 \implies x = 2 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -1$$

Substitute each $x$-value back into $y = x + 2$ to find the coordinates:
$$\text{When } x = 2: y = 2 + 2 = 4 \implies (2, 4)$$
$$\text{When } x = -1: y = -1 + 2 = 1 \implies (-1, 1)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $x^2 = x + 2 \implies x^2 - x - 2 = 0$ and factors to $(x - 2)(x + 1) = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: applying the tangency condition b^2 - 4ac = 0 to find unknown line parameter.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of finding tangent constant using discriminant.

hints: Equate the two equations: $x^2 + 2x + 5 = 4x + k \implies x^2 - 2x + (5 - k) = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the equations and collect terms into standard quadratic form:
$$x^2 + 2x + 5 = 4x + k$$
$$x^2 - 2x + (5 - k) = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition $b^2 - 4ac = 0$:
$$(-2)^2 - 4(1)(5 - k) = 0$$
$$4 - 20 + 4k = 0 \implies 4k = 16 \implies k = 4$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: applying the non-intersection condition b^2 - 4ac < 0 to find parameter range.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of solving for no-intersection range via discriminant.

hints: Equate line and curve: $x^2 + 6x + 7 = 2x + k \implies x^2 + 4x + (7 - k) = 0$.
For no intersection, require the discriminant to be strictly negative: $b^2 - 4ac < 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the intersection quadratic equation:
$$x^2 + 6x + 7 = 2x + k$$
$$x^2 + 4x + (7 - k) = 0$$

Apply the condition for no real intersection ($b^2 - 4ac < 0$):
$$4^2 - 4(1)(7 - k) < 0$$
$$16 - 28 + 4k < 0$$
$$-12 + 4k < 0 \implies 4k < 12 \implies k < 3$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: applying two distinct intersections condition b^2 - 4ac > 0 to find gradient parameter range.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of two distinct intersections via discriminant.

hints: For two distinct intersection points, set $b^2 - 4ac > 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Form the standard quadratic equation for the $x$-coordinates of intersection:
$$x^2 + 4 = mx$$
$$x^2 - mx + 4 = 0$$

Apply the condition for two distinct real roots ($b^2 - 4ac > 0$):
$$(-m)^2 - 4(1)(4) > 0$$
$$m^2 - 16 > 0$$
$$(m - 4)(m + 4) > 0 \implies m < -4 \quad \text{or} \quad m > 4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Forms $x^2 - mx + 4 = 0$ and sets discriminant $b^2 - 4ac = m^2 - 16 > 0$.
Solves quadratic inequality to obtain $m < -4$ or $m > 4$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of line intersecting reciprocal curve.

hints: Equate $3 - x = \dfrac{2}{x}$ and multiply through by $x$.
Substitute $x = 1 \implies y = 2$ and $x = 2 \implies y = 1$ to obtain $(1, 2)$ and $(2, 1)$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the equations and multiply by $x$ (with $x \neq 0$):
$$3 - x = \dfrac{2}{x}$$
$$3x - x^2 = 2$$
$$x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0$$
$$(x - 1)(x - 2) = 0 \implies x = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad x = 2$$

Find the corresponding $y$-coordinates:
$$\text{When } x = 1: y = 3 - 1 = 2 \implies (1, 2)$$
$$\text{When } x = 2: y = 3 - 2 = 1 \implies (2, 1)$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of calculating point of contact of tangent.

hints: Factorise as a repeated root: $(x + 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = -3$.
Substitute $x = -3$ into $y = x^2$ to find $y = 9$, giving $(-3, 9)$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate line and curve and write as a quadratic equation:
$$x^2 = -6x - 9$$
$$x^2 + 6x + 9 = 0$$
$$(x + 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = -3$$

Substitute $x = -3$ into either equation to find $y$:
$$y = (-3)^2 = 9$$
$$(-3, 9)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: simultaneous linear and quadratic equations, forming a standard 3-term quadratic and solving for both intersection points.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming quadratic equation from intersection of line and parabola.

hints: Set the two expressions for $y$ equal to each other: $x^2 - x - 6 = 3x - 1$.
Subtract $3x$ and add $1$ to both sides.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the expressions for $y$ from the curve and the line:
$$x^2 - x - 6 = 3x - 1$$

Rearrange all terms to the left-hand side:
$$x^2 - x - 3x - 6 + 1 = 0$$
$$x^2 - 4x - 5 = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates $x^2 - x - 6 = 3x - 1$ and rearranges to obtain $x^2 - 4x - 5 = 0$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding coordinates of intersection points.

hints: Substitute into $y = 3x - 1$: $x = 5 \implies y = 14$ and $x = -1 \implies y = -4$, giving $(5, 14)$ and $(-1, -4)$.

walkthrough.text:
Factorise and solve the quadratic equation:
$$x^2 - 4x - 5 = 0$$
$$(x - 5)(x + 1) = 0 \implies x = 5 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -1$$

Substitute each $x$-value into the linear equation $y = 3x - 1$:
$$\text{When } x = 5: y = 3(5) - 1 = 14 \implies B(5, 14)$$
$$\text{When } x = -1: y = 3(-1) - 1 = -4 \implies A(-1, -4)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: finding a tangent constant by equating discriminant to zero and calculating the unique point of contact.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding constant for tangency using discriminant.

hints: Equate line and curve: $x^2 - 4x + 12 = 2x + k \implies x^2 - 6x + (12 - k) = 0$.
For a tangent, set discriminant $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the equations to form a single quadratic in $x$:
$$x^2 - 4x + 12 = 2x + k$$
$$x^2 - 6x + (12 - k) = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition $b^2 - 4ac = 0$:
$$(-6)^2 - 4(1)(12 - k) = 0$$
$$36 - 48 + 4k = 0$$
$$4k = 12 \implies k = 3$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding coordinates of point of contact.

hints: Substitute $x = 3$ into $y = 2x + 3$: $y = 2(3) + 3 = 9$, so the point of contact is $(3, 9)$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $k = 3$ into the quadratic equation:
$$x^2 - 6x + (12 - 3) = 0$$
$$x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0$$
$$(x - 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = 3$$

Calculate the corresponding $y$-coordinate:
$$y = 2(3) + 3 = 9$$
$$\text{Point of contact is } (3, 9)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: clearing fractions to form a quadratic from rational curve intersection and applying b^2 - 4ac < 0 to find no-intersection parameter interval.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Clearing rational terms to form quadratic intersection equation.

hints: Add $x$ to both sides to get $4x + \dfrac{4}{x} = k$.
Multiply the entire equation by $x$ and rearrange to get $4x^2 - kx + 4 = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the curve and line expressions for $y$:
$$3x + \dfrac{4}{x} = k - x$$

Add $x$ to both sides and multiply by $x$ (with $x \neq 0$):
$$4x + \dfrac{4}{x} = k$$
$$4x^2 + 4 = kx$$
$$4x^2 - kx + 4 = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates $3x + \dfrac{4}{x} = k - x$, multiplies by $x$, and rearranges to obtain $4x^2 - kx + 4 = 0$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding range of values for no real intersections.

hints: For the line not to meet the curve, the quadratic must have no real roots ($b^2 - 4ac < 0$).

walkthrough.text:
Apply the non-intersection condition $b^2 - 4ac < 0$ to $4x^2 - kx + 4 = 0$:
$$(-k)^2 - 4(4)(4) < 0$$
$$k^2 - 64 < 0$$

Factorise and solve the quadratic inequality:
$$(k - 8)(k + 8) < 0$$
$$-8 < k < 8$$

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $k^2 - 4(4)(4) < 0 \implies k^2 - 64 < 0$ and identifies critical values $\pm 8$.
States final set of values $-8 < k < 8$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: finding two tangent gradients from a fixed y-intercept and evaluating the respective contact points.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding tangent slopes from discriminant equation.

hints: Equate line and curve: $x^2 - 2x + 4 = mx - 5 \implies x^2 - (m + 2)x + 9 = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the equations and collect terms in standard quadratic form:
$$x^2 - 2x + 4 = mx - 5$$
$$x^2 - (m + 2)x + 9 = 0$$

Set the discriminant to zero for tangency:
$$(m + 2)^2 - 4(1)(9) = 0$$
$$(m + 2)^2 = 36$$
$$m + 2 = \pm 6 \implies m = 4 \quad \text{or} \quad m = -8$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding coordinates of contact points for each tangent slope.

hints: State both points of contact: $(3, 7)$ and $(-3, 19)$.

walkthrough.text:
For $m = 4$, solve for the point of contact:
$$x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0 \implies (x - 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = 3$$
$$y = 4(3) - 5 = 7 \implies (3, 7)$$

For $m = -8$, solve for the point of contact:
$$x^2 + 6x + 9 = 0 \implies (x + 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = -3$$
$$y = -8(-3) - 5 = 19 \implies (-3, 19)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: clearing algebraic fraction to obtain a 3-term quadratic, computing discriminant, and solving two-distinct-points inequality.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming quadratic equation and computing discriminant for rational curve.

hints: Equate $-2x + c = \dfrac{8}{x}$ and multiply through by $x$ (with $x \neq 0$).

walkthrough.text:
Equate the equations and clear the denominator:
$$-2x + c = \dfrac{8}{x}$$
$$-2x^2 + cx = 8$$
$$2x^2 - cx + 8 = 0$$

Calculate the discriminant $\Delta$:
$$\Delta = (-c)^2 - 4(2)(8) = c^2 - 64$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates $-2x + c = \dfrac{8}{x}$ and multiplies by $x$ to obtain $2x^2 - cx + 8 = 0$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding range of values for two distinct intersections.

hints: For two distinct intersection points, set the discriminant strictly positive: $c^2 - 64 > 0$.
State the solution as two disjoint inequalities: $c < -8$ or $c > 8$.

walkthrough.text:
For two distinct points of intersection, the discriminant must be strictly positive:
$$\Delta > 0 \implies c^2 - 64 > 0$$

Factorise and solve the quadratic inequality:
$$(c - 8)(c + 8) > 0$$
$$c < -8 \quad \text{or} \quad c > 8$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $c^2 - 64 > 0$ for two distinct intersection points.
Solves quadratic inequality to obtain $c < -8$ or $c > 8$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: quadratic in disguise with u = sqrt(x), solving for non-trivial intersection coordinates, and computing exact distance between intersection points.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving line and square root curve intersection via quadratic substitution.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the expressions for $y$:
$$x - 2 = 4\sqrt{x} - 5$$

Solve the quadratic equation for $u$, then find $x$:
$$(u - 1)(u - 3) = 0 \implies u = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad u = 3$$
$$x = 1^2 = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad x = 3^2 = 9$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $x = u^2$ and $\sqrt{x} = u$ into $x - 2 = 4\sqrt{x} - 5$ to form $u^2 - 4u + 3 = 0$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding full coordinates and exact length of chord segment.

hints: Substitute $x = 1$ into $y = x - 2$ to find $y = -1$, giving $P(1, -1)$.
Substitute $x = 9$ into $y = x - 2$ to find $y = 7$, giving $Q(9, 7)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate $y$-coordinates of points $P$ and $Q$ using $y = x - 2$:
$$\text{When } x = 1: y = 1 - 2 = -1 \implies P(1, -1)$$
$$\text{When } x = 9: y = 9 - 2 = 7 \implies Q(9, 7)$$

Calculate the exact distance between $P(1, -1)$ and $Q(9, 7)$:
$$PQ = \sqrt{(9 - 1)^2 + (7 - (-1))^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{64 + 64} = \sqrt{128} = 8\sqrt{2}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: rational curve tangency, establishing 2nd-degree discriminant condition for horizontal tangents, and solving for coordinates of points of contact.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deriving tangency condition equation for rational curve.

hints: Equate $\dfrac{4x + 3}{x^2 + 1} = c$ and multiply by $x^2 + 1$ to get $4x + 3 = c(x^2 + 1)$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line equation $y = c$ to the curve equation and clear the denominator:
$$\dfrac{4x + 3}{x^2 + 1} = c$$
$$4x + 3 = c(x^2 + 1)$$
$$cx^2 - 4x + (c - 3) = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = 0$:
$$(-4)^2 - 4(c)(c - 3) = 0$$
$$16 - 4c^2 + 12c = 0$$

Divide by $-4$ to obtain the required equation:
$$-4(c^2 - 3c - 4) = 0 \implies c^2 - 3c - 4 = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates $\dfrac{4x + 3}{x^2 + 1} = c$ and rearranges to obtain $cx^2 - 4x + (c - 3) = 0$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving for values of constant and contact points.

walkthrough.text:
Solve the quadratic equation in $c$:
$$c^2 - 3c - 4 = 0$$
$$(c - 4)(c + 1) = 0 \implies c = 4 \quad \text{or} \quad c = -1$$

For $c = 4$, find the point of contact on $y = 4$:
$$4x^2 - 4x + (4 - 3) = 0$$
$$4x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0 \implies (2x - 1)^2 = 0 \implies x = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5$$
$$\text{Point of contact: } (0.5, 4)$$

For $c = -1$, find the point of contact on $y = -1$:
$$-x^2 - 4x + (-1 - 3) = 0$$
$$-x^2 - 4x - 4 = 0 \implies x^2 + 4x + 4 = 0 \implies (x + 2)^2 = 0 \implies x = -2$$
$$\text{Point of contact: } (-2, -1)$$
